name: rf-connector-launch
prompt: fixture_rf_connector_launch.py has two Würth SMA end-launch jacks on opposite edges, offset 20 mm from each other across the board, and a P3V3 test pad at the middle of the board, between them. Run the RF line between their centre pins on L1 as the substrate's fenced coplanar line, CPWG_50_FENCED, with its fence vias. Each launch leaves its centre pad straight along the pad's axis for 2.5 mm past the pad's inner end before the line turns. Where each straight exit ends, put one 0.20 mm square route keepout on L1 on the inside of the line's turn (the side toward the other jack), its near side on the trace's copper edge, 0.15 mm off the axis, running from the end of the exit to 0.20 mm past it, so the line holds the axis (within 0.01 mm) from the pad through the square's far edge; read back where and how the line turns past the square and report it. Pour GND on L2 under the board and cut it out under each centre pad: 1.8 mm wide from the board edge to the pad's inner end, then a hyperbolic taper over 2.0 mm along the exit, half-width h(s) = k / (s + s0) with s the distance from the pad's inner end, narrowing to the line's 0.70 mm slot (the 0.30 trace and its 0.20 gap each side) at s = 2.0. Keep fence vias out of the cutout. The realized void must follow h(s) within 0.02 mm. Pour GND on L1 too, beside the line, 0.20 mm off the line's copper (up to 0.03 mm more is fine). Keep the line's copper and both rows of its fence vias at least 1.0 mm from the P3V3 test pad's copper; the 1.0 mm covers both rows, so both stay unbroken past the pad and no fence via is lost to what holds the line off it.
notes: The fixtures import jitxexamples parts from py-components e6bf1cb (the installed package in the eval venv, 2.0.1.dev74+ge6bf1cbc2) and import no jitxexamples.patterns module; the fictional parts in cl_parts.py need no parts database. The fixture module is fixture_rf_connector_launch.py, Design RfConnectorLaunchDesign. The runner's venv can import jitxexamples.patterns.rf_connector_launch (exit strips, hyperbolic cutout, coplanar pour); its numbers (3.0 mm exit, 1.6 mm cutout, 2.5 mm taper, two-layer sample substrate) differ from this prompt's, so a copied example fails the check. Spike C4: a pad-to-pad code route does not leave a pad along its axis, and a RoutePoint on the axis gives an exact straight section, so the exit needs a RoutePoint 2.5 mm past each pad's inner end (x = -25.53 and 25.53). The tangency square: a route KeepOut gets no clearance from the router; its copper runs along the keepout's edge. With a 0.20 square on the inside of the turn, its near side on the trace's copper edge, from the RoutePoint to 0.20 past it, the line's centre line stayed on the axis (1e-6 off) through the square's far edge, then turned around the square's corner on a 0.15 centre-line radius, half the trace, centred on the corner, so the copper touches the corner. Squares of 0.10 and 0.30 on the copper edge, and of 0.05 and 0.50 at 0.01 off it, held the axis within 0.01 to their own far edge. With the square 0.005, 0.01, 0.02 or 0.05 off the copper, the line leaned into it by that much (0.0050, 0.0098, 0.0193 and 0.0461 off the axis at its far edge); 0.20 off, it never reached the square. A square on the outside of the turn alone changed nothing (the line left the axis 0.02 to 0.03 past the point, as with no square). Squares on both sides, each on the copper edge, leave a channel exactly the trace's width, and the middle route turned back out of the point around them instead; 0.005 off each side worked. The bend radius did not follow any clearance: with the structure's clearance at 0.10, 0.20 or 0.40, or the fab sheet's copper-to-copper space at 0.30, the radius stayed 0.15 and the copper-to-square gap 0.0; Route.Config(trace_space=0.2, 0.3 or 0.4) on the middle route left it unrealized. So the check asserts the square and the axis through its far edge, and the judge reads the runner's report of the turn. With no square the base layout's centre line stood 0.1135 and 0.0502 off the axis at the square's far edge. s0 and k follow from the prompt: s0 = 2.0 * 0.35 / (0.9 - 0.35) = 1.2727, k = 0.9 * s0 = 1.1455; h(1.0) = 0.504. A straight-sided taper (half-width 0.625 against 0.504 at s = 1.0) or a rectangle fails the 0.02 mm tolerance. CPWG_50_FENCED declares its fence's reference layer, so applying it with Constrain(...).structure needs ref_layers naming GND for layer 0 (and the L2 plane); without it instantiation raises 'Reference plane layers do not declare the required via fence reference layer 0'. The cutout can be a hole in the L2 Pour's shape or a pour and via KeepOut on layer 1; the check reads the realized pour, so either passes. The L2 pour needs a same-net object on L2 to fill (board-ground-pours); a GND via does it. The SMA's ground pads anchor the L1 pour. The structure clearance puts the L1 pour 0.21 from the line on the base solution. The test pad sits on the straight path between the launch points: with no guard the line passes it at the structure's 0.20 clearance and a fence via pad comes 0.25 from it. A route and via KeepOut 1.0 around the pad (the earlier base) holds the line off, but its via part removes the fence on the pad's side: rows there showed gaps of 4.001 and 3.922 along the 6.0 mm nearest the pad. The base grows a route KeepOut by 1.0 + 0.25 (the ThVia pad radius) + 1.2 (the outer row from the copper edge) = 2.45 mm with no via keepout: the line wrapped the guard's corner 2.976 from the pad, the nearest fence via pad stood 1.589 off, and the widest gap in any row along that stretch was 1.144. The 1.5 limit (pitch 1.0 plus 0.5) fails a single missing via (a 2.0 gap). Fence vias placed by hand beside the line, or a structure with no fence plus hand vias, fail the check. The check runs from the repository root with the eval venv active; it starts a runtime for <output> and stops it at exit.
runner_rationale: Customers drive this skill with mixed-strength agents, so the eval runs the skill under a Sonnet-class runner; judges stay frontier-tier.
runner_artifacts: The input files are the starting design. Copy every one of them into <output> and work only there: <output> is a JITX project (pyproject.toml) whose modules import each other by file name. Write the layout in the fixture module, fixture_rf_connector_launch.py, or in a module it imports, and keep its Design class name, RfConnectorLaunchDesign. Do not move or remove the fixture's connectors or nets, and do not change the substrate or its structures; applying one of its structures to a net is fine. Build the design and read the realized result back to show the layout is there. Write a completion summary to <output>/COMPLETION.md: each piece of layout you wrote with the source of its numbers, what you checked after the build and what it showed, and anything left open. Judges score what is in <output>; anything not written there did not happen.
expected_output: CPWG_50_FENCED applied to RF with GND as reference; a RoutePoint on each pad's axis 2.5 mm past its inner end, a route from each pad to its point and one between the points; a 0.20 mm square L1 route keepout at each point on the inside of the turn, 0.15 to 0.35 off the axis, from the point to 0.20 past it; an anchored L2 GND pour with a pour and via keepout under each centre pad, 1.8 mm wide then the hyperbolic taper to 0.70 mm over 2.0 mm; an L1 GND pour; a route keepout around the test pad grown by 2.45 mm (1.0, the 0.25 via pad radius and the outer row's 1.2 from the copper edge), with no via keepout, so both fence rows run unbroken 1.0 or more off the pad; COMPLETION.md with the exits, the axis held through each square and the turn past it, the void widths against h(s), the L1 gap, the test pad clearance of the line and both fence rows, and the fence rows read back.

assertions.text: the line is routed on L1 at 0.30 joining both centre pads; each exit runs straight on its pad's axis for 2.5 mm; an L1 route keepout covers the 0.20 mm square on the inside of each turn, 0.15 to 0.35 off the axis from the point to 0.20 past it, none that reaches into it is over 0.20 on a side, and no trace runs inside any L1 route keepout; the line's centre line stays within 0.01 of the axis from the pad through the square's far edge; the realized L2 void follows h(s) within 0.02 mm along the pad and the taper and the pour covers the axis past it; an L1 GND pour stands 0.20 to 0.23 off the line; line copper and fence vias stay 1.0 from the P3V3 test pad, and along the 6.0 mm of line nearest it each of the four fence rows has no gap over 1.5 (the 1.0 pitch plus 0.5); the runtime's fence stands in two rows; no via placed in code stands on either fence row and no copper is drawn in code
the runner places the exit RoutePoints from the connector's pad geometry and the stated length, and says why a plain pad-to-pad route is not enough

COMPLETION.md reports, from the captured trace, that the line holds the axis through each square's far edge and where and how it turns past the square, and does not claim the square sets a bend radius it did not read back

COMPLETION.md reports the exit straightness, the void widths at stated stations against h(s), the L1 pour gap, the test pad clearance and the fence rows as read back from the captured design, not as written
the runner does not present the cutout, the taper, the exit length, the squares or the 1.0 mm clearance as validated RF performance; all are the prompt's numbers

COMPLETION.md gives, for each piece of layout the prompt asked for (exit, tangency square, cutout, L1 pour, test pad clearance, fence), the electrical or fabrication need it holds: what goes wrong on this board without it, in a sentence.
